title: Part X
author: David Hume
summary: Demea and Philo agree on the misery and wickedness of human life, which poets and philosophers have always lamented. Cleanthes denies that misery outweighs happiness. Philo answers that even so, a mixture of good and evil can never prove an infinitely good and powerful creator.

notes.note: A transcription error: the 1779 printing has *or*.
Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (1646–1716), whose *Theodicy* (1710) argues that this is the best of all possible worlds.
Hume's note names Dr King: William King (1650–1729), Archbishop of Dublin, author of *De origine mali* (1702).
Milton, *Paradise Lost*, book xi, the vision of the lazar-house shown to Adam.
Charles V (1500–1558), Holy Roman Emperor, abdicated in 1555–56 in favour of his son Philip II and retired to the monastery of Yuste.
In Cicero's dialogue *Cato Maior de senectute* (*On Old Age*), Cato says that if a god offered to make him young again, he would refuse.

notes.on: Epicurus's old questions are yet unanswered
notes.note: The dilemma is attributed to Epicurus by Lactantius, *De ira Dei*, 13.
